statement: The chart shows the number of rainy days in five months. In which month did the number of rainy days change the most compared with the month before?

figure.alt: A bar chart of rainy days per month, with the scale marked every 2 days and gridlines every day: March 4, April 10, May 12, June 5, July 7.

choices.misconception: I picked the month with the fewest rainy days instead of looking at changes between months.
I only looked at increases, so I found the jump of 6 into April and ignored the bigger drop.
I picked the tallest bar, which shows the most rain, not the biggest change.

choices.text: It cannot be told from the chart
choices.misconception: I thought a bar chart only shows amounts, so I did not see that the changes can be worked out by subtracting.

hints: A change can go up or down.
Read each bar's height carefully from the scale, then subtract each month from the next one. A drop counts as a change just as much as a rise, so compare the sizes of the differences.
The heights are 4, 10, 12, 5 and 7. The changes are 6 up, 2 up, 7 down and 2 up.

solutions.reliable: Reading the bars gives March 4, April 10, May 12, June 5 and July 7. The changes from one month to the next are 6 (into April), 2 (into May), 7 (into June) and 2 (into July). The biggest change is the drop of 7 from May to June, so the answer is June. The transferable idea: a question about change is about the gaps between bars, not the bars themselves, and a fall is as big a change as a rise.
solutions.elegant: Look for the biggest step between neighbouring bar tops: the cliff from the tallest bar, May, down to June stands out at once.

whyOnTest: Charts test whether you read what is asked: the biggest change is a gap between bars, and the tallest bar is the trap.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
